page.layout: One printed column of index entries, with page numbers at its right edge; below it, a second alphabetical list of Italian words with page numbers at the right.; One printed page, index in two columns of entries with page numbers at right, under headings; the page is cut at the right edge so numbers are partly cut off.; Narrow strip of a printed index page: one column of entries at left-centre, with a heading "GERMANICA." centred in the column, and a few partial right-hand columns of page references cut at the right edge; no margin notes.; Two columns of index entries with page numbers at the right, the main column in the centre-right and a fragment of a column of page numbers at the far left edge. Under the main column, the section headings ANGLICA. and ILLYRICA. each stand centred over their own entries. Below the last entry, the word CONRA- stands alone at the foot as a catchword.
page.notes: The Greek entries are transcribed as far as legible; the line "Χαλκὶς ἡ χαλκιδικὴ σαῦ-" continues on the next line as "ex" (partly unclear). Some numbers at the right edge are cropped and uncertain. The right edge of the page is cut off, so the final digits of some page numbers are missing; entries are transcribed as far as visible. Only the left portion of the entries is legible; the right-hand page-reference columns are cut off at the edge, so their numbers are incomplete and are given only where visible (e.g. "ibi", "6", "7", "4"). Some entries are set in black letter (Fraktur) and are transcribed as printed; the ornate letterforms may be imperfectly rendered. The left strip holds only fragments of page numbers from another column, cut at the edge; several are uncertain and the strip's lines could not be matched to entries. The main column is read directly. The catchword CONRA- is set at the foot. The ANGLICA and ILLYRICA headings are taken as level 2 sub-headings of the index.
